content.text:
I'm treating this as one missed RMD: Teodoro's 2025 IRA RMDs were covered, but the $12,729.96 owed from his Calloway 401(k) (SYN-52710004) was never taken from that plan.

**Who owes and when.** Teodoro was born 14 March 1952, so he turned 73 in 2025. That makes 2025 his first RMD year, and its deadline was 1 April 2026. He retired from Calloway Turbine Works in 2019, so the plan's exception for people still working doesn't apply. Marguerite is his sole beneficiary and only about 3½ years younger, so the factor comes from the Uniform Lifetime Table: 26.5 at age 73. Each RMD is the account's value on 31 December 2024 (holdings plus cash) divided by 26.5:

| Account | 31 Dec 2024 value | 2025 RMD |
|---|---|---|
| SYN-52710002 Traditional IRA | $623,678.60 | $23,535.04 |
| SYN-52710003 Rollover IRA | $210,343.76 | $7,937.50 |
| SYN-52710004 Calloway 401(k) | $337,343.96 | $12,729.96 |
| **Total** | | **$44,202.50** |

**What was taken.** On 24 November 2025 Teodoro signed a form asking for one payment from IRA SYN-52710002. On 4 December 2025 that IRA paid out $44,202.50 gross, with $4,420.25 federal tax withheld; the 2025 1099-R matches. That is exactly the total of all three RMDs.

**Why that doesn't cover the 401(k).** IRA RMDs can be combined and taken from any of the person's IRAs, so the $31,472.54 owed by the two IRAs is covered. A 401(k)'s RMD can't be taken from an IRA; it has to come out of the plan itself. The 401(k) had no distribution in 2025 or before 1 April 2026: its transactions and Q1 2026 statement show only dividends and fees. So its RMD was missed in full. The extra $12,729.96 taken from the IRA doesn't count toward it.

You may want to look into having the plan pay out the missed amount and whether the IRS excise tax on it can be reduced or waived; that is outside these files.
